interest: Dutch choice to bury Allied ashes from Fukuoka in Manila.
overview: Despatch of April 27, 1949 from The Hague: the Dutch decline sending Allied ashes from Fukuoka mass graves to the U.S., preferring a Manila cemetery.

subfiles.about: Transmittal of a diplomatic note from the Netherlands Ministry of Foreign Affairs concerning the shipment of Allied war dead ashes from mass graves in Japan.
subfiles.from: Robert D. Coe, Counselor of Embassy, American Embassy, The Hague
subfiles.summary: Coe forwards the Dutch note of April 20, 1949 on shipping Allied ashes from mass graves in Japan.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 180 from Robert D. Coe (The Hague) to Secretary of State on shipment of Allied ashes
subfiles.to: The Secretary of State, Washington, D.C.

subfiles.about: Netherlands diplomatic note declining the transfer of Allied ashes from Fukuoka to the United States and requesting burial in Manila.
subfiles.from: Netherlands Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Legal and Administrative Department
subfiles.summary: The Dutch decline to move Allied ashes from Fukuoka Camps I and IV to the U.S. and ask for burial in a U.S. cemetery in Manila.
subfiles.title: Note No. 22796 from Netherlands Ministry of Foreign Affairs regarding burial of Allied ashes from Fukuoka
subfiles.to: Embassy of the United States of America, The Hague
